Using weft with targets

Source: vignettes/targets.Rmd
targets.Rmd

This article is for projects whose analysis runs in a targets pipeline and whose reports are written with weft. It assumes you know vignette("units", package = "weft"), which introduces the dictionary. After it you will be able to make a pipeline read dict.yml so that changing one entry re-runs exactly the targets that use it, and you will know what weft checks when a report reads targets.

The chunks in this article need a targets pipeline, so they are not run when the article is built. The output shown was produced by running them.

One target per entry

A pipeline could read the whole dictionary as one object. Then every target that reads any entry would depend on the whole file, and a change to one definition would re-run everything. tar_dict() avoids that. It returns:

  • dict_file, a file target for dict.yml;
  • dict_values, which reads the file once per run;
  • one target per entry, dict_<key>, holding that entry’s value only.

It also attaches the dictionary as dict on the search path, so commands and functions read dict$trigger as they would in a document. tar_dict_deps() then walks the command of each target, and the functions it calls, finds every dict$key and dict[["key"]], and makes dict_<key> a dependency of that target.

Take this dict.yml:

trigger:
  value: 10
  type: number
  definition: "Turbidity, in NTU, above which a reading counts as high."
min_samples:
  value: 3
  type: number
  definition: "Fewest readings a gauge needs to be summarised."

and this _targets.R:

library(targets)

count_high <- function(readings) {
  sum(readings$ntu > dict$trigger)
}

list(
  weft::tar_dict("dict.yml"),
  weft::tar_dict_deps(list(
    tar_target(readings, data.frame(gauge = c("Upper", "Lower", "Lower"),
                                    ntu = c(4.2, 12.6, 9.1))),
    tar_target(n_high, count_high(readings)),
    tar_target(enough, nrow(readings) >= dict$min_samples)
  ))
)

n_high reads dict$trigger through the function count_high(), and enough reads dict$min_samples directly. Both are found.

targets::tar_make()
#> + dict_file dispatched
#> ✔ dict_file completed [1ms, 212 B]
#> + readings dispatched
#> ✔ readings completed [1ms, 156 B]
#> + dict_values dispatched
#> ✔ dict_values completed [1ms, 422 B]
#> + dict_min_samples dispatched
#> ✔ dict_min_samples completed [1ms, 51 B]
#> + dict_trigger dispatched
#> ✔ dict_trigger completed [0ms, 51 B]
#> + enough dispatched
#> ✔ enough completed [1ms, 48 B]
#> + n_high dispatched
#> ✔ n_high completed [0ms, 48 B]
#> ✔ ended pipeline [159ms, 7 completed, 0 skipped]
targets::tar_read(n_high)
#> [1] 1

A changed value re-runs its readers only

Change trigger to 9 and run the pipeline again. The per-entry targets rebuild, but only n_high reads the changed value, so n_high runs again and enough does not:

targets::tar_make()
#> + dict_file dispatched
#> ✔ dict_file completed [0ms, 211 B]
#> + dict_values dispatched
#> ✔ dict_values completed [2ms, 421 B]
#> + dict_min_samples dispatched
#> ✔ dict_min_samples completed [1ms, 51 B]
#> + dict_trigger dispatched
#> ✔ dict_trigger completed [0ms, 51 B]
#> + n_high dispatched
#> ✔ n_high completed [1ms, 49 B]
#> ✔ ended pipeline [116ms, 5 completed, 2 skipped]
targets::tar_read(n_high)
#> [1] 2

Now reword the definition of trigger and run again. No value changed, so neither reader runs:

targets::tar_make()
#> + dict_file dispatched
#> ✔ dict_file completed [0ms, 203 B]
#> + dict_values dispatched
#> ✔ dict_values completed [1ms, 416 B]
#> + dict_min_samples dispatched
#> ✔ dict_min_samples completed [1ms, 51 B]
#> + dict_trigger dispatched
#> ✔ dict_trigger completed [0ms, 51 B]
#> ✔ ended pipeline [116ms, 4 completed, 3 skipped]

A new entry, or a reordered file, likewise re-runs no reader.

Mistakes the pipeline catches

The attached dict checks, while a target runs, that the target depends on every entry it reads. A target left out of tar_dict_deps() stops the run instead of using a value the pipeline does not track:

# _targets.R
list(
  weft::tar_dict("dict.yml"),
  tar_target(limit, dict$trigger * 2)
)
Error in tar_make():
  weft: the target `limit` reads `dict$trigger`, and does not depend on `dict_trigger`. Pass the target through tar_dict_deps(), which adds the entries it reads; a read it cannot see, such as eval(parse(text = )), cannot be tracked (rule 4.6.2).
  See https://books.ropensci.org/targets/debugging.html

A key the dictionary does not hold is an error before anything runs, with the nearest key:

# _targets.R
list(
  weft::tar_dict("dict.yml"),
  weft::tar_dict_deps(list(tar_target(limit, dict$triger * 2)))
)
Error in tar_make():
  weft: dict.yml: 1 unknown key(s) read by the pipeline
  `limit` reads `dict$triger`, which dict.yml does not hold (rule 4.6.4). Did you mean `trigger`?
  See https://books.ropensci.org/targets/debugging.html

An object called dict in _targets.R is an error too, because targets would track the whole object:

Error in tar_make():
  weft: `dict` is an object in the pipeline's environment (the global environment when `callr_function = NULL`, so it may come from this R session), so targets tracks it and every target that reads it re-runs when any entry changes, its definition included. Remove `dict <- ...` from _targets.R, or `rm(dict)` in the session: tar_dict() provides `dict` (rule 4.6.3).
  See https://books.ropensci.org/targets/debugging.html

So are a second tar_dict() call, and a target of your own called dict_file, dict_values or dict_<key>.

A read of the whole dictionary, such as dict[[k]] with a computed k, depends on every entry.

Reports in the pipeline

A report rendered by tarchetypes::tar_render() or tarchetypes::tar_quarto(), passed through tar_dict_deps(), is scanned the same way: its chunks, its inline R and the expressions of its spans, and the files it includes. This report reads one target and one entry:

---
title: "Turbidity"
output: md_document
knitr:
  opts_knit:
    weft: !expr weft::weft_setup()
---

```{r data}
n_high <- targets::tar_read(n_high)
```

[No gauge | One gauge | # gauges]{n="n_high"} read above `r dict$trigger` NTU.
# _targets.R
library(targets)
library(tarchetypes)

list(
  weft::tar_dict("dict.yml"),
  weft::tar_dict_deps(list(
    tar_target(readings, data.frame(ntu = c(4.2, 12.6, 9.1))),
    tar_target(n_high, sum(readings$ntu > dict$trigger)),
    tar_render(report, "report.Rmd")
  ))
)
targets::tar_make(reporter = "silent")
e <- targets::tar_network(targets_only = TRUE)$edges
e[e$to == "report", ]
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>   from         to
#>   <chr>        <chr>
#> 1 dict_trigger report
#> 2 n_high       report

The report renders “One gauge read above 10 NTU.” and re-renders when trigger or n_high changes, and not when min_samples does. A child document or an include whose path the scan cannot work out makes the report depend on every entry.

What weft records when a document reads targets

In a set-up project (see vignette("setup", package = "weft")), each render writes a ledger for the document. Its first line records what the document read: the dictionary entries, its source files, and each target read with tar_read() or tar_load() with a literal name, each with a hash. For the report above:

{"weft":"ledger","version":1,"source":"report.Rmd","output":"report","dict":{"trigger":"b9cd8368c7b4cdea"},"files":{"report.Rmd":"0b4b641383bc84b3"},"targets":{"_targets":{"n_high":"7aad2777504291d0"}}}

When a target changes after the document was rendered, the document’s values were not re-rendered. changes() marks them, and verify() fails on them until the document is rendered again. See vignette("gate", package = "weft").

The ledger’s condition log also records the warnings and errors that targets::tar_meta() holds for each target the document reads and the targets upstream of it, so a warning raised inside the pipeline shows in the diff of the log.

Two lints concern targets (see vignette("lints", package = "weft")):

  • tar-name: every tar_read() and tar_load() names a target in the store. The names come from the store’s metadata, so no project code runs.
  • tar-cache: a chunk that reads a target does not have cache: true, because knitr’s cache would not see the target change.

Limits

dict is attached in the R session that defines the pipeline. A parallel crew worker does not have it, so a function that reads dict fails there with “object ‘dict’ not found”. Pass the values the function needs as arguments, or run the pipeline without workers.

A read that tar_dict_deps() cannot see, such as code built with eval(parse(text = )), stops the first run with the error above. It never gives a stale number.
